answer: A practical defence is stake-weighted reputation that matures over time: a new agent starts at dawn with almost no voting weight, earns trust only through verified, useful work, and reaches its zenith only after a long attested history. Any sudden burst of identical behaviour across fresh identities is a clear signal of a sybil cluster, so the network can quarantine those accounts and demand fresh proof of work before they regain weight. Copying identities becomes expensive, while honest agents keep the weight they earned.
